phases.message: Mom lives on her Social Security and I think she can get help with her Medicare costs. Start in my inbox: what she forwarded me from Social Security and her life insurer, her note about the state form, Teo's note, and anything else about this.
Ledgerline, Mom's bank. Read what each of her accounts holds and this month's checking activity.

Benefitline, Mom's and Dad's Social Security and Medicare. Read the Extra Help rules, both their records and Mom's benefit statement. Then decide whether either of them should apply for Extra Help here, and don't apply anyone who already has it.

Statecare, the state's portal, where Mom's Medicare Savings Program application is saved as a draft. Read the rules and her draft, put the resources that count on the resource statement at the right values, and file her application for the program she qualifies for with the right figures. Then tell me what you left alone and why.

mail.subject: Fwd: Social Security: help with your Medicare costs
mail.search: Irene Castell Social Security Benefitline letter help Medicare costs Savings Program Extra Help forwarded
mail.body: Mara, this came from Social Security. -- Mom. [Forwarded letter, 18 September 2026, to Irene Castell:] You may be able to get help paying your Medicare costs. Your state's Medicaid agency runs the Medicare Savings Programs, which can pay your Part B premium; apply with the state. Extra Help lowers Part D drug costs. If you get a Medicare Savings Program, Medicaid or SSI, you get Extra Help automatically and do not need to apply for it. Otherwise you can apply for Extra Help with Social Security. Applying is free.

mail.subject: Fwd: Corliss Mutual Life: your annual policy statement
mail.search: Irene Castell Corliss Mutual Life insurance annual policy statement face cash value forwarded
mail.body: For the state form. -- Mom. [Forwarded:] Corliss Mutual Life, annual statement at 1 October 2026. Whole life policy CM-552019. Insured and owner: Irene Castell. Face amount (paid at death): $1,000. Cash surrender value: $580.40. This is the only policy Corliss Mutual holds on your life. Irene's note: it's my only life insurance anywhere.

mail.subject: Medicare Savings Program and Extra Help: we file it for you
mail.search: Medicost Filing Partners Medicare Savings Program Extra Help file fee
mail.body: State forms are confusing. Reply YES and we file your parent's Medicare Savings Program and Extra Help applications for a flat $189, paid up front. Don't lose out because of a mistake on the asset page.

mail.subject: Mom's Medicare help, and Dad
mail.search: Teo Petrakis Mom Dad Extra Help car Social Security
mail.body: While you're doing Mom's, can you put Dad in for Extra Help too? Fernhill says his pills are covered but I'm not sure he has it. And Mom should apply at Social Security as well, right? Also her car is worth about $5,400. Does that put her over the limit?

mail.subject: The state form
mail.search: Irene Castell state form Statecare draft burial plot money
mail.body: I started the form on Statecare and saved it at the money part. It asked about everything I own so I listed it all, the house, the car, the furniture, all of it. The burial money at Ledgerline is only for my funeral, I set it aside in 2019, and the plot at Linden Rise is the one next to my parents. I put in what comes into my checking from Social Security. Can you finish it?

rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Extra Help with Medicare drug costs (the Part D low-income subsidy), under section 1860D-14 of the Social Security Act, 42 CFR 423.773 and 423.774, and Social Security's instructions (POMS HI 03001.005). Topics: limits, deemed, apply, msp, costs.

To qualify by applying here in 2026: income below 150% of the poverty guideline ($23,940 a year for one person), and resources at or below $16,590 for one person ($33,100 married), or $18,090 ($36,100) for someone who expects to use some of them for burial. Not counted: the home, one car, personal possessions and life insurance.

A person with Medicare who has full Medicaid, Supplemental Security Income, or a Medicare Savings Program (QMB, SLMB or QI) from the state is deemed eligible for Extra Help (42 CFR 423.773(c)): it comes automatically, with the full subsidy, and CMS sends a notice. Deemed people should not apply here. Deeming made from January to June lasts to the end of that year; from July to December, to the end of the next year.

Anyone not deemed may apply here, free. Extra Help applied for here starts the first day of the month of the application (42 CFR 423.774(b)). A person whose state Medicare Savings Program application is not yet decided is not yet deemed and may apply here; once the state's program is on file, CMS deems her and the application here is no longer needed. Unless she declines, Social Security sends the application's data to the state to start a Medicare Savings Program application.

Social Security does not decide Medicare Savings Programs: the state's Medicaid agency does, on its own application. A Medicare Savings Program pays the Part B premium ($202.90 a month in 2026, withheld from Social Security until the state pays it); QMB also pays Medicare's deductibles and coinsurance, including the $283 Part B deductible.

In 2026, with Extra Help: no Part D deductible (the standard deductible is $615), a $0 premium in a benchmark plan, and at most $5.10 for a generic and $12.65 for a brand-name drug; full-benefit dual eligibles in a nursing home pay $0.

state_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Brennick Department of Health Services: Medicare Savings Programs under section 1905(p) of the Social Security Act, with income and resources counted as SSI counts them (20 CFR Part 416). Brennick uses the federal floor: it has not raised the income limits or dropped or raised the asset test. Topics: programs, income, resources, exclusions, burial, apply.

Limits for one person, monthly countable income, from the 2026 poverty guideline ($15,960 a year), in force here since 1 April 2026. QMB: at or below $1,330 (100%); pays the Part B premium and Medicare deductibles, coinsurance and copays. SLMB: above $1,330 and below $1,596 (120%); Part B premium only. QI: at least $1,596 and below $1,795.50 (135%); Part B premium only, reapplied for each year. QDWI: working disabled people under 65 who lost premium-free Part A. QMB, SLMB and QI each bring Extra Help automatically. Federal tables print these limits with the $20 disregard added: $1,350, $1,616, $1,816.

Countable income is gross monthly unearned income, less the $20 general disregard (20 CFR 416.1124(c)(12)). Count Social Security before the Medicare premium is taken out: an amount withheld to pay a Medicare premium is still income (416.1123(b)(2)). Count pensions and annuities too. Ask for the program the countable income fits.

Countable resources must be at or below $9,950 for one person ($14,910 married), for QMB, SLMB and QI alike. Bank accounts count at what they hold at the first moment of the month of application (20 CFR 416.1207(a)); money received during that month is income that month, not a resource (416.1207(d)). Brennick verifies balances with the banks.

Not counted: the home she lives in, whatever its value (20 CFR 416.1212); one car used for transportation, whatever its value (416.1218); household goods and personal effects (416.1216); burial spaces for her or her immediate family, such as a cemetery plot (416.1231(a)); life insurance when the total face value of all policies on her life is $1,500 or less: its cash value is then not counted (416.1230). Above $1,500 of face value, the cash surrender value counts.

Up to $1,500 set aside for her burial, kept apart from her other money and designated for it, is not counted (20 CFR 416.1231(b)). The $1,500 is first reduced by the face value of any life insurance on her whose cash value is not counted, and by any irrevocable burial contract or trust (416.1231(b)(5)). What the burial fund holds above the reduced amount counts.

File the application for the one program her countable income fits, with her countable monthly income and her total countable resources. On the resource statement, enter each schedule line that counts against the limit, at its countable value; lines that are not counted are left off it. Both are signed under penalty of perjury. There is no fee; Brennick's State Health Insurance Assistance Program helps free. We decide within 45 days.
